newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's banking activity up in August.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's banking activity up in August.

text.p: The consolidated balance sheet of Lebanon's commercial banks rose 1.27 percent in August to 32,892 billion Lebanese pounds, the Bank of Lebanon said in its latest monthly bulletin.
Total deposits in foreign currencies and Lebanese pounds rose 2.15 percent to 27,342 billion pounds from 27,048 billion in July, it said.
Lebanese pound deposits grew 2.25 percent to 11,243 billion pounds from 10,995 billion a month earlier.
Deposits in foreign currencies rose 0.62 percent to $10.307 billion in August compared with $10.247 billion in July, the Bank added.
Dollarisation of bank deposits dropped slightly to 58.88 percent from July's 59.35 percent. The dollarisation rate stood at 66.57 percent at the end of August 1995.
Loans and credits to the private sector rose 0.09 percent in August over July, increasing to 11,774 billion pounds.

Credits in Lebanese pounds rose 1.3 percent in August to 1,587 billion from 1,567 billion pounds a month earlier. Credits in foreign currencies rose 0.20 percent to $6.522 billion from $6.509 billion.
Dollarisation of credits fell to 86.52 percent from 86.68 percent at the end of July, the Bank said.
